claim: The adaptive traffic signal system operates through an emergent collective intelligence mechanism where intersections follow simple local rules that, when combined with neighbor communication, result in system-wide optimization without explicit coordination.
mechanism: Each intersection follows simple local rules: if queue length is above threshold, increase green time proportionally to queue length; if throughput is below threshold, adjust offset to better match neighbor phases. These rules, combined with limited neighbor communication about phase timing, create an emergent system that self-organizes to optimize network flow. The system exhibits properties similar to slime mold network formation, where simple components create complex adaptive behavior.
evidence: Emergence in biological systems like slime mold networks
Success of simple rule-based systems in complex environments (e.g., ant colonies)
Empirical observation that traffic systems can self-organize under certain conditions
assumptions: Local rules are sufficient for system-wide optimization
Neighbor communication provides enough information for coordination
The system will exhibit emergent properties beyond the sum of individual behaviors
Simple rules can adapt to diverse traffic conditions
expected_failure_modes: Failure to adapt to unusual traffic patterns not represented in the rule design
Emergence of unwanted collective behaviors like phantom traffic jams
Sensitivity to initial conditions leading to different outcomes for similar scenarios
novelty_rationale: This hypothesis proposes an emergent intelligence approach rather than an optimization-based one, potentially offering more robust adaptation to unexpected conditions by relying on simple, distributed rules rather than complex calculations.
testability: The hypothesis can be tested by implementing the simple rules in simulation and measuring whether system-wide optimization emerges. The rules can be systematically varied to identify which combinations produce the best results.
falsifier: If the system fails to achieve network-wide optimization under diverse conditions, or if performance degrades compared to centrally optimized solutions even with sufficient time for emergence, the emergent intelligence mechanism would be falsified.
